content.abstract:
A Comparative Study of VLF Signals
from Several Transmitters around the World
as Observed from Maitri Station, Antarctica
Sudipta Sasmal1, Sandip K. Chakrabarti1,2 and Sujay Pal2
1Indian Centre for Space Physics, Kolkata
2 S. N. Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences, Kolkata
ABSTRACT
To examine the behavior of the sunrise and sunset terminators, characteristics of the
solar activities in the polar region and the possible seismic correlation with ionospheric
anomalies a Stanford AWESOME VLF receiving system was installed at the Indian
permanent Antarctic station Maitri during the 27th Indian scientific expedition to Antarctica.
Almost five weeks of data was recorded successfully from several transmitters around the
globe. The narrow-band signals show variation of the solar radiation and the signature of
the prolonged day and night. W e compare the signal of frequency 18.2 kHz with the same
signal received at Kolkata and we present simultaneous observation of the variation of the
sunrise and sunset terminators. W e compare the diurnal signal amplitude variation with
the LWPC model. W e also present the broadband signal, contains the signature of sferics.
The signals do not have a strong signature of whistlers because at the conjugate points, the
lightning effects are minimum.
Keywords: VLF Signals, Comparison, Maitri Antarctica, Kolkata India.
1.0  INTRODUCTION
Electromagnetic wave of radio frequency range 3 to 30 kHz is known
as Very Low Frequency or VLF. The ionosphere of upper atmosphere of
earth is a good reflector of VLF wave and that is why VLF signal propa-
gates nicely through earth-ionosphere waveguide. Electron and ion den-
sity profile, structural and chemical properties of the stratified layers of
the ionosphere change with diurnal and seasonal variations of the solar
radiations and other earth related natural activities. During the propaga-
tion, VLF signal modifies itself accordingly and carries ionospheric infor-
mations corresponding to these changes. This is why VLF radio electro-
magnetic wave analysis is very significant method for understanding the
behavior and the physical and chemical configuration of the ionospheric
layer structures.

Lon. 77°44¢). In Antarctica, the major objective was to study of the signal
variation over very long path which is totally over the ocean. During this
observation, we have chosen the summer period of the southern
hemisphere in such a way that we got the "full day and no night" (no true
sunset) condition as well as the true sunset condition. Figure 1 shows the
